findings.title: The 0.65.0 copier fix reads `mv` as a copy, so the strict bash guard now permits moving any file OUT of the checkout — including hooks/ itself — a shape it explicitly denied one commit earlier
evidence: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:47 puts `mv` in `_COPIERS` alongside cp/install/rsync/ln, and hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:370-386 `_check_copier` yields only the destination: "`cp SRC... DST` writes DST and reads the rest". That is true of cp and false of mv — mv's source is removed, not read.

DIFFERENTIAL, the same four commands against the hook at the previous commit and at HEAD, fed the hook its own PreToolUse payload with VERDICT_STRICT=1 and cwd=checkout. At 1ae041c (`git show 1ae041c:hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py` into a scratch dir): all four DENY(2). At HEAD 5dc59fb: all four ALLOW. The four are `mv <checkout>/src/verdict_mcp/state.py <scratch>/stolen.py`, `mv -t <scratch> <checkout>/src/verdict_mcp/state.py`, `mv <checkout>/hooks <scratch>/hooks_gone`, and `rsync -a --remove-source-files <checkout>/src/ <scratch>/m/`.
The third of those moves the guard's own directory out of the checkout, so the control can now be removed by a command the control permits.

The denial that used to catch it is still in the suite and still green, because it never exercised this direction: tests/test_hooks.py:274 parametrizes `"mv a.py b.py"` with relative operands, which resolve against the checkout, so the destination rule alone still denies it. Every mv/ln/install/rsync case in that table (lines 274-284, 308) has an in-checkout destination.

The three tests added for the fix (tests/test_hooks.py:514-544) cover `cp` only: copy out, copy in, and `-t DIR`. No test in the repository exercises `mv`, `rsync --remove-source-files`, `ln` or `install` through the new `_check_copier` path — `grep -n -e "mv " -e rsync -e "install " tests/test_hooks.py` returns lines 274, 276, 284, 308 (the old table) and 515 (a docstring).

Scope of the hole, measured on the same probes: writing INTO the checkout is still refused in every form tried — `cp -a`, two-source `cp`, `cp -t`, `cp --target-directory=`, `cp -aT`, `rsync`, `ln -sf`, `install -m 644`, and plain `rm -rf <checkout>/src` all DENY(2). The regression is confined to the source operand of the copier path.

root_cause.mechanism: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:359-360 routes every `_COPIERS` head to `_check_copier`, which yields exactly one target (the last operand, or `-t`'s argument) and drops the rest as read-only sources. For `mv` and for `rsync --remove-source-files` the source operand is written — it is deleted — so dropping it drops the only check that was protecting it.
root_cause.origin: 4da9ed3 (v0.65.0, "which test, and who chose it"), the VERDICT-F-37 fix. Before it, hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:354-357 yielded every non-flag argument of every `_MUTATORS` head, which caught the source by accident rather than by design.

class.pattern: a mutator whose non-last operand is also written
sites: searched `_COPIERS` = {cp, mv, install, rsync, ln}: `cp`, `install` and `ln` genuinely only read their sources; `mv` always removes its source; `rsync` removes its source under `--remove-source-files`. Two of the five are wrong, and both were confirmed ALLOW at HEAD by probe.

the sibling arms are position-aware and unaffected: `_check_tar` (:350), `_check_find` (:352), the stream editors (:237). The blanket `_MUTATORS` fallback at :361-364 still yields every operand for rm/rmdir/unlink/touch/mkdir/chmod/chown/truncate/shred/tee/patch.

root_cause.latent_condition: the mutator denial table (tests/test_hooks.py:262-311) uses relative operands throughout, so every command in it has an in-checkout destination. A change to source handling cannot fail any test in that table — the suite could not have caught this.

The resolution stands, deliberately.

src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:1123-1132 (`_stamp_outcome`) then reads the same record, sees `at_head == "fail"`, sets `contradicts`, and returns `{"outcome": "unknown", "outcome_reason": "claimed fix-verified, but the cited test still fails at HEAD"}`. It never looks at `not_weighed`.

PROBE against both shipped functions in sequence, one finding, one record: after `_apply_verification` the entry is status `resolved`, delta `RESOLVED`, fix_verified True, with `not_weighed` = "chosen by prose order from 3 cited tests — too weak to refuse a resolution; cite `verification_test` to make it count". `_stamp_outcome` on that same entry returns `{"outcome": "unknown", "outcome_reason": "claimed fix-verified, but the cited test still fails at HEAD"}`. Two consumers of one record, opposite conclusions, in one run.
The published reason is also untrue as written: "the cited test" was not cited for this finding — the harness's own record says nobody chose it.

NEW IN THIS RANGE rather than pre-existing. At 1ae041c there was no `not_weighed` arm: an at_head `fail` reopened the finding unconditionally (delta became STILL_OPEN), so `_stamp_outcome` took the still-open path and no contradiction was possible. 0.65.0 created the half-state in which a finding is resolved and its ledger row is denied.

Direction of the error is the safe one — a hand-verified resolution is understated as undecided rather than overstated as confirmed — which is why this is Minor and not Major. It would rise to Major on evidence of a live occurrence: a cited test that fails at HEAD while the suite is green (an order-dependent or standalone-failing test). This run has none: the suite is 639 passed, exit 0.

Class link, searched rather than asserted: `not_weighed` is written at harness.py:566 and read nowhere — `grep -rn 'not_weighed' src/verdict_mcp/` returns exactly one hit, the write. findings.title: The VERDICT_STRICT bash guard reads shell metacharacters inside quoted strings and heredoc bodies as live syntax and resolves phantom targets against the checkout, blocking read-only QA commands
evidence: UNTOUCHED IN THIS RANGE for this mechanism: the only change to hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py in 1ae041c..HEAD is the `_COPIERS` block (lines 43-49 and 359-386). The redirection scan and the segment splitter are byte-identical.

RE-PROVEN THREE TIMES THIS SESSION, each on a read-only command, with the checkout unmodified throughout. (1) `echo "${VERDICT_HOME:-<unset>}"` — the placeholder word in angle brackets was read as an output redirection and refused with "output redirection targets '<checkout>/}'". That was the first command of the run.

(2) A heredoc whose Python body contained a probe string with `&& cp ...` inside an f-string literal: the segment splitter treated the `&&` inside the quoted body as a command separator and refused with "cp targets '<checkout>/{repo}/src/x.py'" — resolving a phantom path that still contains the literal `{repo}` brace, which is proof the text was never a command.

(3) NEW SHAPE, not previously recorded: `grep -n "mv \|rsync\|ln -\|install " tests/test_hooks.py` — a grep alternation. The `|` characters inside the quoted pattern were read as pipes, making `install " tests/test_hooks.py` a segment, and the command was refused with "install targets '<checkout>/tests/test_hooks.py'". So it is not only `>` and `<`: quoting is invisible to the segment splitter as well as to the redirection scan, and an alternation regex containing any mutator word is refused.

The blocked shapes are ordinary in read-only QA work: grep alternations are the standard way to search for several patterns at once, and this session used one to establish the test-coverage gap in VERDICT-F-39.

COST, measured: three retries this session, each one round trip and a reworded command; every finding was still obtained. It stays Minor for that reason. It would rise to Major if a project's only route to a piece of evidence went through a blocked shape — restated from run 7 and still not met.
